st.headline: Tesla teases imminent launch of Cybercab ‘robotaxi’
st.teaser: The gold-coloured vehicle can carry two passengers and marks the first Tesla car with no steering wheel or pedals.
fullText: NEW YORK – Electric vehicle-maker Tesla is teasing the upcoming debut of its self-driving robotaxi , dubbed “Cybercab”, to compete with the likes of Uber and Waymo.
The Elon Musk-founded company shared a promotional image on social media late on Aug 21 promising “exclusive access” to Cybercabs at a Sept 3 event in Austin, Texas, where Tesla is headquartered.

“We’re celebrating the launch of our Cybercab robotaxi with an exclusive event in Austin – and you could be there,” the company said on its website, promoting a sweepstake to win a chance to attend the event.
First unveiled in October 2024, the gold-coloured vehicle can carry two passengers and marks the first Tesla car with no steering wheel or pedals.
At the time, Musk said the company was planning to begin production of the self-driving cars before 2027 and sell them to private buyers for under US$30,000 (S$38,000).

US tech industry publication The Information reported earlier that Tesla staffers have been told the roll-out will begin with Cybercab rides for employees on public roads, followed by the vehicle being incorporated into the ranks of its Robotaxi service in Austin.
Tesla enthusiasts have in recent weeks reported seeing parking lots filled with Cybercabs, sparking rumours of an impending launch.
In 2025, Tesla debuted its self-driving cars in Austin using its Model Y SUV vehicles, with the “Robotaxi” service gradually expanding to several other cities in Texas, Florida and California.
However, state laws require many of the vehicles to have a human supervisor or driver ready to take over control if necessary.
Waymo, the self-driving vehicle subsidiary of Google parent company Alphabet, offers its services in 11 US cities. AFP

cna.headline: Bangladesh 39-3 at lunch, trail by 107 runs in second test v Australia
cna.teaser: Bangladesh 39-3 at lunch, trail by 107 runs in second test v Australia
fullText: Aug 23 : Bangladesh were 39 for three in their second innings at lunch on day two of the second test against Australia in Mackay on Sunday, trailing by 107 runs.

• Australia paceman Mitchell Starc took two wickets in successive balls, having opener Shadman Islam caught for one before bowling Mominul Haque for a duck when the number three failed to play a shot.
• Opener Tanzid Hasan was caught for nine by Starc at deep fine leg after a miscued pull shot off the bowling of captain and fast bowler Pat Cummins.
• Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto was 23 not out at the break, with number five batter Mushfiqur Rahim on four at Great Barrier Reef Arena.

• Bangladesh's recalled fast bowler Shoriful Islam took a seventh wicket after dismissing Cameron Green lbw for 67 with an in-swinging yorker. Shoriful finished with 7-48, the best innings haul for a Bangladesh bowler in an away test.

• Tailenders Nathan Lyon (32 not out) and Josh Hazlewood frustrated Bangladesh with a 24-run partnership for the 10th wicket before Hazlewood was caught for six by Shadman after top-edging an attempted slog-sweep off left-arm spinner Taijul Islam.
• Bangladesh lead the two-match series 1-0 after thrashing Australia by nine wickets in Darwin.
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

economistArticle.title: The Toll of the Tariff Wall
paras: As Donald Trump's proposed trade policies loom over global markets, economists are racing to quantify the ultimate damage of a heightened tariff regime. With America's global effective tariff rate potentially scaling to a historic 10.0%, the ramifications will reverberate far beyond Washington. For highly open, trade-dependent economies like Singapore, any disruption to the flow of global commerce behaves like an economic tremor, threatening supply-chain stability and raising import costs across the board.

The mechanism of modern protectionism is deceptive; while it promises to shield domestic manufacturers, it often triggers retaliatory tariffs from trade partners. This tit-for-tat escalation threatens to fragment global supply chains that have taken decades to optimize. Multinational corporations, accustomed to seamless cross-border logistics, now face the daunting task of rearranging their production networks, a process that is both capital-intensive and highly inflationary.

In Southeast Asia, the consequences are multifaceted. While some nations might witness a short-term windfall as businesses relocate manufacturing hubs to bypass American duties, the overall contraction in global demand is bound to dampen growth. Singapore's status as a premier financial and logistics hub makes it particularly vulnerable to a slowdown in aggregate trade volume. When global shipping lanes quiet down, the island's port and maritime services feel the pinch almost immediately.

Moreover, higher tariffs serve as a regressive tax on consumers. As intermediate goods become pricier, manufacturers invariably pass these costs down the value chain, culminating in elevated retail prices. Central banks worldwide, having just brought inflation under control after a grueling post-pandemic cycle, may find themselves forced to keep interest rates higher for longer to combat this new wave of supply-side inflation.

Ultimately, an era of double-digit effective tariffs risks dismantling the multilateral trading system that has underpinned global prosperity for half a century. As unilateral barriers replace rules-based cooperation, smaller nations must navigate a highly polarized economic landscape. For Singapore, survival in this fragmented environment will require relentless innovation, a deepening of regional trade agreements, and an agile shift toward higher-value services.
economistArticle.cn:
随着唐纳德·特朗普拟议的贸易政策笼罩全球市场，经济学家们正争分夺秒地量化关税提高所带来的最终损害。由于美国的全球实际关税率可能飙升至历史性的10.0%，其影响将远远超出华盛顿的范围。对于像新加坡这样高度开放、依赖贸易的经济体而言，全球商业流动的任何中断都像是一场经济余震，威胁着供应链的稳定并全面推高进口成本。

现代保护主义的机制具有欺骗性；虽然它承诺保护国内制造商，但往往会引发贸易伙伴的报复性关税。这种针锋相对的升级威胁到几十年优化而成的全球供应链面临分崩离析。习惯了无缝跨国物流的跨国公司，现在面临着重组生产网络的艰巨任务，这一过程既需要资本密集，又会带来高度通胀。

在东南亚，后果是多方面的。虽然一些国家可能会因为企业转移制造基地以规避美国关税而获得短期意外收益，但全球整体需求的收缩势必会抑制增长。新加坡作为主要的金融和物流枢纽，使其特别容易受到总贸易量下滑的影响。当全球航运航线归于沉寂时，这座岛国的港口和海运服务几乎会立即感受到压力。

此外，更高的关税对消费者而言相当于一种累退税。随着中间品变得更加昂贵，制造商不可避免地会将这些成本沿着价值链向下转嫁，最终导致零售价格高企。全球央行在经历了艰难的疫情后周期并刚刚将通胀控制住之后，可能会发现自己不得不更长时间地维持高利率，以应对这一新一轮的供给侧通胀。

归根结底，双位数实际关税时代的到来，存在着拆毁支撑了半个世纪全球繁荣的多边贸易体系的风险。随着单边壁垒取代基于规则的合作，较小的国家必须在高度两极分化的经济版图中艰难前行。对于新加坡而言，在这一碎片化的环境中生存，将需要不懈的创新、加深区域贸易协定以及敏捷地向高价值服务转型。
